newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DUBAI-BASED DOLPHIN INVESTS IN S.AFRICA ECOTOURISM.
newsitem.headline: DUBAI-BASED DOLPHIN INVESTS IN S.AFRICA ECOTOURISM.

text.p: The Dubai-based Dolphin Group launched a joint venture company with South Africa's Mpumalanga Parks Board on Thursday to capitalise on the region's prized ecotourism market.

Under the union between the parastatal and Dolphin, a major player in Africa's leisure industry through its Block Hotels and United Touring Company, the multi-national takes over commercial running of the board's tourism and marketing divisions.

A primary objective of the 400 million rand joint venture is to ensure that South Africa's youngest parks board can become self-sufficient despite progressively dwindling state funds, while keeping a tight rein over the region's rich natural heritage.
Over 2,000 beds for theme camps and lodges are planned under the initial project which envisages four years of construction, with resultant spinoffs for the local building and service industries.
The Mpumalanga provincial government has agreed to underwrite and provide infrastructure to support the emerging programme through the company, Likusasa Lemvelo ("Tomorrow's Nature").
Parks Board chief executive Alan Gray said in a statement that without private sector intervention, conservation in the province would face an uncertain future.
"It is inappropriate to play the purist when considering the region's development pressures," Gray acknowledged.
"The future, we believe, lies in cooperation where the benefits derived from tourism can be shared by developers, the parks board and the community in a...permanent partnership."

New developments will centre on the historic miners' town of Pilgrim's Rest, the majestic Blyde river canyon -- a massive red sandstone gorge with cliff faces plunging 700 metres in parts -- and the Loskop dam reserve.

The Natal Parks Board, also tasked with making ecotourism pay, said last month it was considering linking up with the privately-owned Conservation Corporation to list the Greater St Lucia wetlands on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
